If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–3% starting at mid-horizon (8–14 days) to capture sentiment momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for late horizon (15–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for late horizon (15–30 days) to avoid premature bottoming.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 within 2 days, apply a +2% correction to forecast at mid-horizon (8–14 days) to reflect strong bullish sentiment.
